Commentary.Commentary: Now, it is on to their batters who haven't had the best of times in this series. They have a stiff task. Can they do well this time? Lanka on the other hand, will back themselves to defend this. Stay tuned for the chase.

West Indies let them down in the field! They dropped a lot of catches and had that been taken, things could have been different. Amongst the bowlers, Joseph was good at the end and Forde was brilliant at the start. Motie was yet again economical but the others leaked runs.

That's a fine, fine innings from Mendis, he rode his luck but he has provided the much-needed impetus his side needed. Lanka courtesy him, have got to a very good score. Before that, it was tough going for them, they did not lose wickets but the going was slow. Then there was a long rain break and the game was reduced to a 23-per over side game. Lanka though managed to score over 70 runs in the last five.
That's brilliant fielding but excellent running too! Full and outside off. This is hit wide of long off. The fielder runs there, dives and stops it. They take three though.

We have a time! The game is to resume at 1520 GMT and it is going to be a 23-over per side game! Total entertainment. Here we go..:
UPDATE - 1455 GMT - The rain has stopped and the covers are also off! We should get in a game if there is no more rain. Fingers crossed.

UPDATE - 1413 GMT - The last a game can start is 1540 GMT, that will be a 20-over game. The chances though look bleak as the rain is still coming down and the ground will take sometime to be ready for a game.
UPDATE - 1313 GMT - The covers are back on again! The rain isn't heavy but it is consistent. The wait goes on...
UPDATE - 1252 GMT - The rain has stopped again and the covers are coming off AGAIN! Let's hope it stays away for good now.

UPDATE - 1205 GMT - Well, the covers did come off for a while but they are back on again and the rain has returned! Doesn't seem very heavy, the ground staff are still on the ground but the covers are firmly in placed. Well, scratch what we just wrote, more covers are being got on and the rain has got heavier.
UPDATE - 1142 GMT- It's been more than an hour now since the delay and we just might start losing overs! Well, just as we write that, we have some very good news coming in, THE COVERS ARE COMING OFF!
UPDATE - 1100 GMT - Nothing new to update for now, it continues to rain and the covers are firmly on. The waiting game continues.
UPDATE - (1014 GMT) - The heavens have opened up! It's coming down quite steadily and it has got really dark. The covers have now come on.

TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and will bowl first!

It gets better and better for Sri Lankan team who have yet again seen off another series win and this time against the might Windies who started the tour with a T20I win but since then it has gone downhill for them. They lost the other two T20I matches, resulting in series loss and have been beaten comprehensively so far in the ODI series. Their batting is what have let them down so far. In both the matches, apart from Sherfane Rutherford we haven't seen much from West Indies and they'll hope they can leave the tour avoiding a whitewash. Pallekele is all set to host the final match. Can West Indies improve with the bat or we will see the spin dominated Sri Lankan team clean sweep the series? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up.
...MATCH DAY...

We are down to the third and final ODI of the series between Sri Lanka and the West Indies at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. After clinching the first T20I in Dambulla, the tourists have struggled, losing four consecutive games across formats, conceding both the T20I and ODI series. As they take the field one last time on this tour, the West Indies will be desperate for a consolation win to salvage some pride. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka will be eyeing a clean sweep to build momentum ahead of their upcoming series against New Zealand next month. In the rain-affected second ODI, Sri Lanka's spinners once again took control, exposing the West Indies' vulnerability to spin, a consistent problem throughout the tour. A late rescue act from Sherfane Rutherford and Gudakesh Motie added some respectability to the visitors' total, but Sri Lanka comfortably chased it down with 5.4 overs to spare. For the West Indies, underperforming key players like Alick Athanaze, Brandon King, and Shai Hope will need to step up if they are to avoid another defeat. Sherfane Rutherford, who has been the standout performer with the bat, will look to continue his excellent form. On the bowling front, Gudakesh Motie has been the most effective, while Alzarri Joseph has been solid but lacked support from others like Hayden Walsh and Jayden Seales. As for Sri Lanka, both their batting and bowling departments have clicked in unison, giving them an edge throughout the series. With the series already in the bag, Sri Lanka may look to rotate their squad to manage workloads ahead of the full-fledged white-ball series against New Zealand. Opener Pathum Nissanka, who missed the first two ODIs due to a quadriceps strain, could return if fit. Fast bowlers Mohamed Shiraz and Dilshan Madushanka, who have yet to feature in the series, could also get a look in for the final ODI, as could uncapped batting all-rounder Chamindu Wickramasinghe. Will the hosts complete a clean sweep? Or will West Indies end the tour with a win? We shall find out.
